findings.issue: The CLI entry-point guard compares import.meta.url (realpath) with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) (unresolved). Invoked through a symlinked absolute path, the guard is false, the script does nothing and exits 0, so the lint guard passes silently.
findings.evidence: Probe: tree with 'x 2.ts'; `node <symlink-to-repo>/tools/lint/sync-copies.js <tree>` exits 0 with no output, while `node tools/lint/sync-copies.js <tree>` exits 1 naming it. `npm run lint` uses a relative path resolved against the physical cwd, so the normal path is unaffected. The idiom is shared with 7 other tools/ scripts and was prescribed by the spec.
findings.fix: Optional: compare against realpathSync(process.argv[1]) (or accept as the project-wide idiom and leave it). Not required for this task.

summary: All six SPEC items implemented as specified and each test would fail on a broken implementation (matcher table, walker dir-once/sort, CLI exit+stderr incl. negatives, sandbox npm run lint, gitignore check-ignore + ls-files -ci empty + no tracked basename matches, README phrases). Regex probes: 'x 10.md' matches, 'foo 2.test.ts' does not (correct: iCloud would name it 'foo.test 2.ts'). Walker skips .git/node_modules at any depth, doesn't follow symlinks (Dirent.isDirectory false), builds POSIX relative paths so Windows separators are irrelevant. Lint ordering is first in the chain. README accurate. Check runs in ~33 ms. Only MINOR/NIT findings.
